text: You’re designing a Power BI report for a sales team. The goal is to help them quickly identify top-performing regions, detect unusual sales spikes, and compare actual sales against targets. You want to make the report visually intuitive and highlight key insights without requiring users to dig through raw numbers. Which of the following techniques should you use to meet these goals? (Select all that apply)

options.text: A. Conditional formatting
options.explanation: Conditional formatting allows you to visually highlight high and low sales values by applying color codes. This technique helps users quickly identify the top-performing regions and detect unusual sales spikes without having to analyze raw numbers. Apply Conditional Table Formatting in Power BI - Power BI | Microsoft Learn

options.text: B. Overlaid analytics
options.explanation: Overlaid analytics, such as average and target lines on charts, provide a visual reference point for users to compare actual sales against targets. This technique helps users easily see how their performance aligns with set goals. With the Analytics pane, you can create the following types of dynamic reference lines: X-Axis constant line Y-Axis constant line Min line Max line Average line Median line Percentile line Symmetry shading Use the Analytics pane in Power BI Desktop - Power BI | Microsoft Learn

options.text: C. Anomaly detection
options.explanation: Anomaly detection flags unexpected sales spikes, helping users quickly identify unusual patterns in the data. This technique allows users to focus on key insights without having to manually search for anomalies. Anomaly detection tutorial - Power BI | Microsoft Learn

options.text: D. Drillthrough filters
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Drillthrough filters allow users to navigate to detailed region pages for more in-depth analysis. While this can be useful for exploring specific data points, it may not be the most effective technique for quickly identifying top-performing regions and unusual sales spikes. Drillthrough in Power BI Reports: Navigate to Detailed Insights - Power BI | Microsoft Learn

options.text: E. Specialized visuals like KPIs and gauge charts
options.explanation: Specialized visuals like KPIs and gauge charts are designed to display performance indicators in a visually intuitive way. Using these visuals can help highlight key insights and compare actual sales against targets without users needing to dig through raw numbers.

options.text: F. Data masking to hide sensitive sales figures
options.explanation: Data masking is used to hide sensitive sales figures, which may not directly contribute to the goal of helping users quickly identify top-performing regions, detect unusual sales spikes, and compare actual sales against targets. While data masking is important for data security, it may not be the most relevant technique for this specific scenario.

explanation: Phrases from Learning Path: Highlighting values in reports helps to quickly communicate important and relevant facts about data. Power BI supports several techniques to highlight values: Conditional formatting Overlaid analytics Anomaly detection Specialized visuals Keep in Mind: Conditional formatting Adds colors, icons, or data bars to show high, low, or special values in tables and charts. Overlaid analytics Adds lines like average, minimum, maximum, or forecast directly on visuals to show trends or targets. Anomaly detection Automatically finds unusual data points, like sudden spikes or drops in a chart. Specialized visuals Uses visuals like KPIs, gauges, and cards to show key numbers clearly and quickly. References: Design reports to highlight values - Training | Microsoft Learn

options.text: A. Background color to highlight cells based on sales performance

options.text: B. Font color to emphasize top-selling products

options.text: C. Data bars to show sales volume visually within cells

options.text: D. Icons to flag stores below target sales

With this approach, you can apply rules to highlight specific cells by using: Background color Font color Data bars Icons Keep in Mind: Used in tables and matrix visuals Helps highlight specific cells based on rules. Supports multiple formatting styles Background color: Shades cells based on value Font color: Changes text color to emphasize values Data bars: Adds horizontal bars to show magnitude Icons: Displays symbols like arrows or flags for performance Rules can be based on values, measures, or field comparisons You can set thresholds or use dynamic logic. section: Model data with Power BI
text: You are designing a Power BI report that includes multiple visuals layered on top of each other. You want to create a guided user experience where clicking a button reveals a specific visual while hiding others. Which bookmark option should you enable to ensure that the visibility of visuals is captured and applied correctly?

options.text: A. Data Bookmark
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. The "Data" bookmark option is not related to controlling the visibility of visuals in a Power BI report. It is used to capture the state of the data displayed in the report, rather than the visibility of visuals.

options.text: B. Current page
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. The "Current page" bookmark option is used to capture the current page layout and settings in a Power BI report. It does not specifically control the visibility of visuals in the report.

options.text: C. Display Bookmark
options.explanation: The "Display" bookmark option is the correct choice for controlling the visibility of visuals in a Power BI report. By enabling this option, you can ensure that the visibility settings of visuals are captured and applied correctly when navigating through different stages of the report. Create report bookmarks in Power BI - Power BI | Microsoft Learn

options.text: D. All visuals
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. The "All visuals" bookmark option is not designed to control the visibility of visuals in a Power BI report. It captures the state of all visuals on the report page, but it does not specifically address the requirement of revealing specific visuals while hiding others for a guided user experience.

explanation:
Why correct

The Display option in bookmarks captures the visibility state of visuals on a report page. This is essential when you want to show or hide specific visuals as part of a guided experience, such as toggling between charts or creating a custom navigation flow.

Why others are wrong

A. Data = This captures the state of filters, slicers, and visuals' data context, not their visibility.

B. Current page = This captures the active page but not the visibility of individual visuals.

D. All visuals = This option applies the bookmark to all visuals but does not specifically control visibility unless Display is selected.

Keep in Mind:

Bookmarks can capture multiple states: data, display, and page.

Display state controls which visuals are shown or hidden.

Use Display when layering visuals or creating toggle buttons.

Display state is essential for storytelling and guided navigation.

You can manually show/hide visuals before saving a bookmark.

Bookmarks can be linked to buttons for interactive navigation.

Use Selection Pane to manage visual visibility.

Display state does not affect filters or slicers.

Always test bookmarks to ensure they behave as expected.

You can update bookmarks to reflect new display settings.

Types of bookmarks:

Data bookmark: Captures the current filter and slicer selections.

Display bookmark: Captures which visuals are visible or hidden.

All bookmark: Captures both filters/slicers and visual display settings.

Exam Tips: Understand the difference between Data, Display, and Current Page options in bookmarks. Practice using the Selection Pane to control visual visibility. Use bookmarks to create interactive reports and guided experiences. Remember that Display is key when toggling visuals. Combine bookmarks with buttons for dynamic navigation. Test each bookmark to ensure it captures the intended state. Know how to update bookmarks after making changes. Use bookmarks to simulate drill-through or page navigation. Be familiar with how bookmarks interact with slicers and filters. Expect scenario-based questions involving layered visuals and user interaction.

text: At Infosys, Meera is designing a report to display key business metrics. She wants to show the current value of total revenue, and also highlight how it compares to a target over time. Which visual should Meera use to meet both requirements?

options.text: A. Card
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. A Card visual is typically used to display a single, high-level metric or value. While it can show the current value of total revenue, it may not be the best choice to compare it to a target over time as it lacks the ability to show trends or historical data.

options.text: B. KPI
options.explanation: A KPI (Key Performance Indicator) visual is the most suitable choice for Meera's requirements. It can display the current value of total revenue and also provide a target comparison over time. KPI visuals are designed to show key metrics and their performance against predefined targets, making them ideal for Meera's report design.

options.text: C. Table
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. A Table visual is used to display detailed data in a tabular format. While it can show the current value of total revenue, it may not be the best choice to visually highlight the comparison to a target over time. Tables are more suited for displaying raw data rather than comparing metrics.

options.text: D. Gauge
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. A Gauge visual is typically used to show progress towards a goal or target. While it can visually represent the current value of total revenue, it may not be the most effective choice for comparing it to a target over time. Gauges are more suitable for displaying single, static values rather than trends or historical comparisons.

explanation:
KPI visuals show a current value, a target, and a time-based trend, making them ideal for performance tracking.

Card visuals only display a single value without comparison or trend context.

Table and Gauge visuals are not designed for showing time-based performance against a target.

Keep in Mind:

What is a Card visual used for?

A Card visual displays a single data point, such as total revenue or number of customers. It does not show comparisons or trends.

What is a KPI visual used for?

A KPI visual shows a current value, compares it to a target, and includes a time-based trend to track performance.

Can a Card visual show variance or progress?

No. Card visuals are static and do not include target or time context.

What are the required fields for a KPI visual?

You need a value, a target, and a time series to configure a KPI visual.

When should I use a KPI instead of a Card?

Use a KPI when you want to show progress toward a goal or compare actual performance against a target over time.

Exam Tips: Know the difference in purpose: Card for single values, KPI for performance tracking Understand the required fields for KPI visuals: value, target, and time Expect scenario-based questions asking which visual best fits a business need Practice configuring both visuals in Power BI Desktop Be ready to identify visuals based on their features and use cases

text: You can configure slicer responsiveness directly within the mobile layout view in Power BI. True or False?

options.text: True
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. There is no direct option to configure slicer responsiveness within the mobile layout view in Power BI. This functionality is not available in the mobile layout view for slicers.

options.text: False
options.explanation: Configuring slicer responsiveness directly within the mobile layout view in Power BI is not possible. Slicer responsiveness settings need to be adjusted in the desktop layout view before publishing the report to ensure proper functionality on mobile devices.

explanation: Slicer settings, including responsiveness and orientation, must be configured in the regular report authoring mode. The mobile layout view only allows rearranging visuals. When you are working in Power BI, you can set up slicers (the filters you use in reports). Things like how the slicer looks (orientation: horizontal or vertical) and whether it adjusts to different screen sizes (responsiveness) must be set up in the normal report editing mode. The mobile layout view is different, it only lets you move visuals around to fit better on a phone screen. You cannot change slicer settings there. So: Regular report mode = where you configure slicer settings. Mobile layout view = where you arrange visuals for mobile, but not change slicer behavior. References: Optimize reports for mobile use - Training | Microsoft Learn

text: You’ve published a Power BI report that users say is slow to load and respond. Your manager asks you to identify which visuals or DAX formulas are causing the delay. You open the report in Power BI Desktop and want to analyze how each element performs during user interaction. What is the most appropriate tool to use first?

options.text: A. Query Diagnostics
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Query Diagnostics is a tool used to analyze the performance of queries and data loading in Power BI. While it can provide valuable insights into data retrieval and transformation processes, it may not directly help in identifying which visuals or DAX formulas are causing the delay in user interaction.

options.text: B. Performance Analyzer
options.explanation: Performance Analyzer is the most appropriate tool to use first when analyzing the performance of visuals and DAX formulas in Power BI reports. It allows you to track the performance of each element during user interaction, helping you pinpoint the specific areas causing the delay.

options.text: C. DAX Studio
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. DAX Studio is a powerful tool for optimizing DAX queries and formulas in Power BI. While it can help in improving the efficiency of DAX calculations, it may not be the most suitable tool for identifying performance issues related to visuals or overall report loading.

options.text: D. Report Usage Metrics
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Report Usage Metrics provides insights into how users interact with your Power BI reports, such as which visuals are being viewed and how often. While it can be useful for understanding user behavior, it may not directly help in identifying the root cause of performance delays in report loading.

explanation: Phrase from the Learning Path: To investigate the cause of poor performance, your first step is to use Performance Analyzer. Performance Analyzer is built-in to Power BI Desktop. It allows you to examine how each of your report elements, such as visuals and DAX formulas, perform. It provides you with logs that measure (in time duration) how each of your report elements performs when users interact with them. By examining the durations in the logs, you can identify which report elements are the most (or least) resource intensive. Why correct Performance Analyzer is built into Power BI Desktop and is specifically designed to measure how visuals and DAX formulas perform during user interactions. It logs the duration each element takes to render, helping you identify bottlenecks and optimize report design. Why others are wrong A. Query Diagnostics = Useful for analyzing query behavior but not focused on visual or DAX performance during interaction. C. DAX Studio = A powerful external tool for deep DAX analysis, but not integrated into Power BI Desktop for visual performance tracking. D. Report Usage Metrics = Provides high-level usage data (views, shares) but not performance diagnostics. Exam Tips: Know where to find Performance Analyzer in Power BI Desktop. Understand what each log entry represents (DAX, visual, other). Practice using it to simulate user clicks and interactions. Be able to distinguish between Performance Analyzer and external tools like DAX Studio. Expect scenario questions involving slow reports and diagnostic steps. Learn how to interpret duration logs to identify performance issues. Remember that Performance Analyzer is for interactive performance, not backend query tracing. Use exported logs for documentation or deeper review. Know when to use Performance Analyzer vs. Query Diagnostics. Always validate performance improvements after changes. References: Tune report performance - Training | Microsoft Learn

section: Model data with Power BI
text: At Wipro, Ramesh is designing a Power BI report. He wants to highlight only the best-performing product categories without showing all the data. He also needs to apply advanced filtering that goes beyond what slicers can do, while keeping the report canvas clean. Which capability in the Filters pane allows Ramesh to achieve this requirement?

options.text: Relative date filtering
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Relative date filtering is not unique to the Filters pane in Power BI. It can also be applied using date slicers or directly within the visuals. While the Filters pane does offer relative date filtering, it is not a capability exclusive to this feature.

options.text: Single selection
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Single selection is a common filtering option available in various parts of Power BI, including slicers, visuals, and the Filters pane. It allows users to select only one item at a time for filtering purposes. While the Filters pane does support single selection, it is not a unique capability of this feature.

options.text: Top N filtering
options.explanation: Top N filtering is a unique capability to the Filters pane in Power BI. It allows users to filter data based on the top N values within a specific category, such as top 10 sales regions or top 5 products by revenue. This feature helps users focus on the most significant data points without cluttering the report canvas with unnecessary details.

explanation:
Why this is correct

Top N filtering is a capability that is only available in the Filters pane. It allows users to filter visuals based on the top or bottom values of a measure, such as top 10 products by sales.

Why the others are wrong

Relative date filtering: This is not unique to the Filters pane. Slicers also support relative date filtering, such as "last 30 days" or "next month".

Single selection: This feature is available in slicers, where users can restrict selection to one item at a time. It is not exclusive to the Filters pane.

Keep in Mind:

What is the Filters pane used for?

It allows report designers to apply filters at the report, page, and visual levels without placing slicers on the canvas.

What types of filters can be applied in the Filters pane?

Basic filters, advanced filters, relative date filters, and Top N filters.

Can slicers perform Top N filtering?

No. Top N filtering is only available in the Filters pane.

Is the Filters pane visible to report consumers?

Yes, unless hidden by the designer. Consumers can interact with it if permissions allow.

Can the Filters pane be customized?

Yes. Designers can format it, lock filters, and control visibility.

Exam Tips: Know which filtering features are unique to the Filters pane Understand the difference between slicers and filters pane capabilities Expect scenario-based questions comparing filter tools Practice applying Top N filters in Power BI Desktop Be familiar with how filters affect visuals, pages, and entire reports

section: Model data with Power BI
text: At Infosys, Neha is designing a report and wants to include an interactive filtering tool that fits neatly into a landscape layout on the report canvas. She also wants users to filter by date and explore top-performing categories. Which of the following capabilities is unique to slicers?

options.text: Horizontal orientation
options.explanation: Horizontal orientation is a layout feature unique to slicers. Slicers in Power BI offer the unique capability of being oriented horizontally, allowing them to fit neatly into a horizontal layout on the report canvas. This orientation makes it easier for users to interact with the filtering tool and navigate through the report effectively.

options.text: Relative date filtering
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Relative date filtering is not a capability unique to slicers in Power BI. This feature allows users to filter data based on relative dates such as "last month" or "last year" and can be applied using other filtering tools or functions within Power BI, not just slicers. Create a Relative Date Slicer or Filter in Power BI - Power BI | Microsoft Learn

options.text: Top N filtering
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Top N filtering, which allows users to filter data based on the top N values in a specific category, is not exclusive to slicers in Power BI. This filtering option can be applied using other visualization tools and functions in Power BI to explore and analyze top-performing categories.

explanation:
Horizontal orientation is a layout feature that is only available in slicers. It allows users to display filter options side by side, which is useful for compact or visually balanced designs.

Why the others are wrong:

Relative date filtering: This is not unique to slicers. The Filters pane also supports relative date filtering.

Top N filtering: This feature is only available in the Filters pane, not in slicers.

Keep in Mind:

What is a slicer in Power BI?

A slicer is a visual filter that allows users to interactively select values to filter data across visuals in a report.

What types of slicers are available?

Power BI supports several slicer types including list, dropdown, date, numeric range, and hierarchy slicers.

Can slicers be oriented horizontally?

Yes. Slicers can be displayed in both vertical and horizontal layouts. Horizontal orientation is unique to slicers and useful for compact designs.

Do slicers support relative date filtering?

Yes. Date slicers can be configured to show relative periods like "last 7 days" or "next month." However, this feature is also available in the Filters pane.

Can slicers perform Top N filtering?

No. Top N filtering is only available in the Filters pane, not in slicers.

How do slicers differ from filters?

Slicers are placed directly on the report canvas and are visible to users. Filters (in the Filters pane) can be hidden and apply at report, page, or visual level.

Can slicers be synced across pages?

Yes. Power BI allows slicer synchronization so that selections made on one page can affect visuals on other pages.

Are slicers affected by Row-Level Security (RLS)?

Yes. Slicers reflect only the data available to the user based on RLS rules defined in the semantic model.

Can slicers be customized?

Yes. You can format slicers with custom fonts, colors, orientation, and selection behavior (single or multiple).

When should I use a slicer instead of a filter?

Use slicers when you want users to interact directly with filtering options on the report canvas, especially for frequently changed filters like dates, categories, or regions.

section: Model data with Power BI
text: Which of the following statements about the Filters pane in Power BI is correct? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: A. Visual-level filters can use measures to eliminate groups
options.explanation: Visual-level filters in Power BI can indeed use measures to eliminate specific groups of data based on the defined conditions. This allows for more granular control over the data displayed in individual visuals.

options.text: B. Page-level filters override report-level filters
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Page-level filters in Power BI do not override report-level filters. Report-level filters are applied first, followed by page-level filters, and finally visual-level filters. This hierarchical order ensures that filters are applied in a consistent manner across the report.

options.text: C. Report-level filters apply to all pages and visuals
options.explanation: Report-level filters in Power BI apply to all pages and visuals within the report. They provide a way to set filters that affect the entire report, ensuring consistency in data representation across different pages and visuals.

options.text: D. Visual-level filters are visible only when a visual is selected
options.explanation: Visual-level filters in Power BI are indeed only visible when a visual is selected. This allows users to focus on specific data points within a visual and apply filters that are relevant to that particular visual without affecting others.

options.text: E. Page-level filters apply to all visuals across all pages
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Page-level filters in Power BI apply only to the visuals on the specific page where the filter is set. They do not automatically apply to all visuals across all pages in the report. Each page can have its own set of page-level filters that impact the visuals displayed on that page.

explanation: Why these are correct A: Visual-level filters can use measures to filter out groups, such as excluding items below a threshold. C: Report-level filters apply globally to all pages and visuals in the report. D: The visual-level filter section appears only when a visual is selected. Why the others are incorrect B: Page-level filters do not override report-level filters; they add to them. E: Page-level filters apply only to visuals on the same page, not across all pages. Keep in Mind: What are the three sections of the Filters pane? Filters on all pages: Report-level filters that apply to all visuals and pages. Filters on this page: Page-level filters that apply only to visuals on the current page. Filters on this visual: Visual-level filters that apply only to the selected visual. Can filters from different levels be combined? Yes. Filters stack from report-level to page-level to visual-level. For example, if a report-level filter limits data to India, a page-level filter to Maharashtra, and a visual-level filter to Mumbai, the final result will show only Mumbai data within Maharashtra in India. What is a use case for report-level filters? A company wants all pages in a report to show data only for the current fiscal year. Applying a report-level filter ensures consistency across the entire report. What is a use case for page-level filters? A sales dashboard has separate pages for each region. Page-level filters can restrict each page to its respective region without affecting other pages. What is a use case for visual-level filters? A column chart shows store performance. A visual-level filter can exclude stores with sales below ₹1,00,000 using a measure like TotalSales. Can visual-level filters use measures? Yes. This is a unique capability of visual-level filters. For example, you can filter out visuals where TotalProfit < 50000 using a measure-based condition. When is the "Filters on this visual" section visible? Only when a visual is selected in the report canvas. It allows fine-tuned filtering specific to that visual. Can filters be locked or hidden from report viewers? Yes. Designers can lock filters to prevent changes or hide them from the Filters pane to simplify the viewer experience. Are filters affected by Row-Level Security (RLS)? Yes. Filters operate on the data available to the user based on RLS rules. If RLS restricts a user to South India, filters will only apply within that subset. What happens if a filter excludes all data for a user? The user will see blank visuals. This often happens when a slicer or filter is set to a value the user doesn’t have access to due to RLS. Can filters be applied dynamically? Yes. You can use DAX measures, slicers, and bookmarks to create dynamic filtering experiences tailored to user selections. How do filters differ from slicers? Filters are managed in the Filters pane and can be hidden or locked. Slicers are visible on the report canvas and allow users to interact directly with filtering options. Exam Tips: Understand the three filter levels: report-level, page-level, and visual-level. Know how each one scopes its effect across the report. Memorize that report-level filters apply to all pages and visuals, page-level filters apply only to visuals on the current page, and visual-level filters apply only to the selected visual. Know that filters stack, not override. For example, a visual can be affected by all three levels simultaneously. Recognize that visual-level filters are the only ones that can use measures to filter groups (e.g., filter out stores with low sales). Expect scenario-based questions that test your ability to choose the correct filter level for a business need. Practice identifying when filters might result in blank visuals, especially when combined with Row-Level Security (RLS). Be familiar with how to access and configure each filter level in the Filters pane. Understand the difference between slicers and filters pane: slicers are interactive visuals on the canvas, while filters pane settings can be hidden or locked. Use Power BI Desktop to experiment with filter combinations and observe how they affect data visibility. Types of filters in Power BI reports - Power BI | Microsoft Learn Resources

text: You’ve built a Power BI report for desktop users and now need to optimize it for mobile devices. Your goal is to ensure that the report is easy to navigate and interact with on phones and tablets. Which of the following actions should you take to create a mobile-friendly experience? (Select all that apply)

options.text: A. Use the mobile layout view to arrange visuals on a phone canvas
options.explanation: Using the mobile layout view to arrange visuals on a phone canvas allows you to optimize the report for smaller screens, ensuring that visuals are displayed in a user-friendly way on mobile devices.

options.text: B. Add new visuals directly to the mobile layout that aren’t in the desktop view
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Adding new visuals directly to the mobile layout that aren't in the desktop view may lead to inconsistencies between the desktop and mobile versions of the report, potentially causing confusion for users.

options.text: C. Choose slicers that are touch-friendly and easy to interact with
options.explanation: Choosing slicers that are touch-friendly and easy to interact with enhances the user experience on mobile devices, making it easier for users to filter and navigate the report on phones and tablets.

options.text: D. Rely solely on responsive visuals in the desktop layout
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Relying solely on responsive visuals in the desktop layout may not be sufficient for creating a truly mobile-friendly experience, as the layout and functionality may not translate effectively to smaller screens.

options.text: E. Test the mobile layout using the Power BI mobile app
options.explanation: Testing the mobile layout using the Power BI mobile app is essential to ensure that the report functions as intended on mobile devices, allowing you to identify and address any issues before sharing the report with mobile users.

explanation: To create a mobile-optimized version of your report, you can: Design a mobile layout view, where you can drag and drop certain visuals onto a phone emulator canvas. Use visuals and slicers that are suitable for use on small, mobile screens. To publish a mobile-optimized version of your report, you simply publish the report as you did previously. The web and mobile versions are published together at the same time. Why correct A. The mobile layout view allows you to drag and drop visuals onto a phone-sized canvas, optimizing layout for small screens. C. Touch-friendly slicers improve usability on mobile devices, making it easier for users to filter data. E. Testing with the Power BI mobile app ensures your layout behaves as expected on actual devices. Why others are wrong B. You cannot add new visuals directly to the mobile layout; only visuals from the desktop layout can be used. D. Responsive visuals help but do not replace the need for a dedicated mobile layout. They adjust size but not layout or interaction design. Keep in Mind: Mobile layout is accessed via the View tab in Power BI Desktop. Only visuals from the desktop layout can be used in mobile layout. Mobile layout does not affect desktop layout. Use slicers that are easy to tap and interact with. Avoid cluttering the mobile canvas with too many visuals. Responsive visuals resize but don’t optimize layout. Mobile layout improves usability and accessibility. Test the mobile layout using the Power BI mobile app. Use the Selection Pane to manage visibility. Mobile layout is essential for executive dashboards viewed on the go. References: Optimize reports for mobile use - Training | Microsoft Learn

text: You are preparing a Power BI report for executives who will access it primarily on mobile devices. One slicer allows filtering by region. You want the slicer to adapt to screen size and show fewer options when space is limited. What configuration should you apply?

options.text: A. Set slicer orientation to vertical
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Setting the slicer orientation to vertical will not help the slicer adapt to screen size and show fewer options when space is limited. This configuration will keep the slicer in a vertical layout regardless of the screen size, which may not be optimal for mobile devices with limited space.

options.text: B. Enable responsive slicer and set orientation to horizontal
options.explanation: Enabling responsive slicer and setting the orientation to horizontal is the correct configuration to apply in this scenario. This setting allows the slicer to adapt to different screen sizes, showing fewer options when space is limited, which is ideal for mobile devices. Horizontal orientation is more suitable for mobile screens as it utilizes the available width efficiently.

options.text: C. Use a dropdown slicer with single-select enabled
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Using a dropdown slicer with single-select enabled may help conserve space on the report page, but it does not address the need for the slicer to adapt to screen size and show fewer options when space is limited. This configuration may not provide the best user experience for executives accessing the report on mobile devices.

options.text: D. Disable responsiveness in the slicer format settings
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Disabling responsiveness in the slicer format settings will prevent the slicer from adjusting to different screen sizes and showing fewer options when space is limited. This configuration will keep the slicer static and may not be suitable for executives accessing the report primarily on mobile devices.

explanation: Learning path is the fundamental for PL300. Each and evry word is important. From there different variety of questions can be asked. Phrase from the Learning path: Decide on the orientation of the slicer, whether it should be vertical, horizontal, or responsive (responsive slicers must be horizontal). If you make the slicer responsive, as you change its size and shape, it shows more or fewer options. If you make the slicer small enough, it becomes a filter icon on the report page. Why correct - Responsive slicers must be horizontal to adapt to screen size. They dynamically adjust the number of visible options and collapse into a filter icon when space is tight. Why others are wrong A. Vertical slicers cannot be responsive. C. Dropdown slicers are static and do not adapt to screen size. D. Disabling responsiveness prevents dynamic adjustment, which is essential for mobile usability. References: Optimize reports for mobile use - Training | Microsoft Learn

text: Match the use case with the correct filter type. Use Cases: Show only products in the "Electronics" category; Display transactions from the last 30 days; Show top 5 cities by total sales; Display customers whose purchase amount is greater than ₹10,000. Filter Types: A. Top N. B. Advanced. C. Relative date and Relative time. D. Basic.

1 - D. Basic

2 - C. Relative date and Relative time

3 - A. Top N

4 - B. Advanced
options.explanation: This is the correct match. Check explanation for more details. Types of filters in Power BI reports - Power BI | Microsoft Learn

options.text:
1 - B. Advanced

2 - A. Top N

3 - C. Relative date and Relative time

4 - D. Basic
options.explanation: This match is incorrect.

explanation:
Show only products in the "Electronics" category - Basic

Basic filters allow you to include or exclude specific values from a field.

Example: Filter the ProductCategory field to show only "Electronics".

Display transactions from the last 30 days - Relative date and Relative time

Relative filters are used to dynamically filter data based on time windows like "last 30 days", "next 1 week", etc.

Example: Filter the TransactionDate field to show only records from the last 30 days.

Show top 5 cities by total sales - Top N

Top N filters allow you to rank values based on a measure and return the top or bottom N items.

Example: Filter the City field to show only the top 5 cities based on TotalSales.

Display customers whose purchase amount is greater than ₹10,000 - Advanced

Advanced filters allow you to apply conditions using operators like greater than, less than, equals, etc.

Example: Filter the PurchaseAmount field where value is greater than ₹10,000.

Keep in Mind:

What is a Basic filter?

Filters specific values from a field.

Use Case: Show only "Electronics" in a product category.

Example: ProductCategory = "Electronics"

What is an Advanced filter?

Allows filtering using logical conditions like >, <, =, contains, etc.

Use Case: Show customers with purchases over ₹10,000.

Example: PurchaseAmount > 10000

What is a Top N filter?

Filters the top or bottom N items based on a measure.

Use Case: Show top 5 cities by sales.

Example: Top 5 City by TotalSales

What is a Relative date or time filter?

Filters data based on dynamic time ranges like "last 7 days", "next month", etc.

Use Case: Show transactions from the last 30 days.

Example: TransactionDate in the last 30 days

Can I use Top N filtering in slicers?

No. Top N filtering is only available in the Filters pane.

Can I use relative date filtering in both slicers and filters?

Yes. Both support relative date filtering.

Can I combine multiple filter types?

Yes. You can apply different filters at report, page, and visual levels, and they stack together.

text: You want to customize how visuals interact with each other on a Power BI report page. Specifically, you need to disable cross-filtering between two visuals and change another interaction to use cross highlighting. Which action should you take?

options.text: A. Use the Format pane to disable cross-filtering
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Using the Format pane allows you to customize the appearance of visuals, such as changing colors or fonts. However, it does not provide an option to disable cross-filtering between visuals on a Power BI report page.

options.text: B. Apply a page-level filter to control visual behavior
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Applying a page-level filter can control which data is displayed on a specific page, but it does not directly impact the interaction between visuals on the page.

options.text: C. Edit visual interactions by selecting the source visual and adjusting interaction icons
options.explanation: Editing visual interactions by selecting the source visual and adjusting interaction icons is the correct action to take in order to customize how visuals interact with each other on a Power BI report page. This allows you to disable cross-filtering between two visuals and change another interaction to use cross highlighting. Change how visuals interact in a report - Power BI | Microsoft Learn

options.text: D. Change the data model relationships between the visuals
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Changing the data model relationships between visuals can impact how data is connected and displayed in Power BI, but it does not specifically address customizing how visuals interact with each other on a report page.

explanation: 1. What is cross-filtering in Power BI? Cross-filtering occurs when selecting a data point in one visual automatically filters other visuals on the same report page. 2. How is cross-highlighting different from cross-filtering? Cross-highlighting emphasizes related data in other visuals without removing unrelated data, whereas cross-filtering hides unrelated data entirely. 3. Can users control visual interactions? Yes. Designers can customize how visuals interact using the Edit interactions feature. 4. How do you access visual interaction settings? Select a visual - Go to the Format tab - Choose Edit interactions - Adjust icons (filter, highlight, none) for each target visual. 5. Can multiple visuals apply cross-filtering at once? Yes. Users can hold Ctrl while selecting multiple visuals to apply layered cross filters. 6. How do you remove a cross-filter? Click the selected data point again or click outside the visual to clear the selection. 7. Do visual interactions apply across report pages? No. Visual interactions are limited to visuals on the same report page. Keep in Mind: If you want the selected visualization to cross-filter one of the other visualizations on the page, select the Filter icon in the upper right corner of that visualization . You can only cross-filter line charts, scatter charts, and maps. You can't cross-highlight them. If you want the selected visualization to cross-highlight one of the other visualizations on the page, select the Highlight icon . If you want the selected visualization to have no impact on one of the other visualizations on the page, select the None icon

text: You are designing a Power BI report and want to use buttons to enhance user experience and interactivity. Which of the following are valid use cases for buttons in Power BI? (Select all that apply)

options.text: A. Navigate between report pages
options.explanation: Using buttons to navigate between report pages is a valid use case in Power BI to enhance user experience and interactivity. It allows users to easily switch between different sections of the report for better data exploration.

options.text: B. Trigger bookmarks to show or hide content
options.explanation: Buttons can be used to trigger bookmarks in Power BI, showing or hiding specific content based on user interactions. This helps in creating dynamic and interactive reports that provide more insights to users.

options.text: C. Apply filters directly to visuals
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Applying filters directly to visuals is not a valid use case for buttons in Power BI. Filters can be applied using slicers or other interactive elements, but buttons are not typically used for this purpose.

options.text: D. Drill through to detailed pages
options.explanation: Using buttons to drill through to detailed pages is a valid use case in Power BI to provide users with more in-depth information on specific data points. It allows users to explore data at a granular level for better analysis.

options.text: E. Export report data to Excel
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Exporting report data to Excel is not a valid use case for buttons in Power BI. Export functionality is typically handled through the Power BI interface and does not require the use of buttons.

options.text: F. Display help overlays or tooltips
options.explanation: Displaying help overlays or tooltips using buttons is a valid use case in Power BI to provide additional information or guidance to users. This can help users understand the data better and make more informed decisions while interacting with the report.

explanation: A. Navigate between report pages - Buttons can be configured with page navigation actions to move between report tabs. B. Trigger bookmarks to show or hide content - Buttons can activate bookmarks that reveal overlays, switch visuals, or toggle visibility. D. Drill through to detailed pages - Buttons can be placed near visuals to initiate drillthrough actions. F. Display help overlays or tooltips - Buttons can show contextual help using overlays or tooltips for built-in assistance. Why others are wrong: C. Apply filters directly to visuals - Buttons don’t apply filters; slicers and filter panes are used for that. E. Export report data to Excel - Exporting is done via the Power BI menu, not through buttons. References: Design reports for navigation - Training | Microsoft Learn

text: You are building a Power BI report for a data analyst who needs to explore granular records, investigate anomalies, and perform analysis for operational data. Which report layout should you choose?

options.text: A. High-level metrics report
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. A high-level metrics report typically provides an overview of key performance indicators and summary data. It does not offer the level of detail required for exploring granular records, investigating anomalies, or performing deep dives into operational data.

options.text: B. Supporting visuals report
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. A supporting visuals report may include additional charts, graphs, or visualizations to complement the main report. While it can enhance the overall presentation, it may not provide the necessary depth for exploring granular records or investigating anomalies.

options.text: C. Detailed report with drill-through options
options.explanation: A detailed report with drill-through options allows the data analyst to navigate through different levels of detail, investigate anomalies, and perform deep dives into operational data. This layout provides the flexibility and interactivity needed to explore data thoroughly.

options.text: D. Executive summary dashboard
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. An executive summary dashboard typically offers a high-level overview of key insights and metrics for quick decision-making by executives. It does not offer the level of detail required for exploring granular records or investigating anomalies in operational data.

explanation: In Power BI report design, a guided analytical experience helps users navigate data in a structured way. It typically includes three levels: High-level metrics = These are summary indicators like KPIs or totals, ideal for executives who need quick insights without diving into details. Supporting visuals = These include charts and graphs that help managers understand trends, comparisons, and performance across categories. Details, when required = This level provides granular data like tables or drill-through views, useful for analysts who need to investigate specific records or patterns. Exam Tips: Executive Leadership is best matched with High-level metrics because they focus on strategic outcomes. Department Manager fits with Supporting visuals to monitor performance and make operational decisions. Data Analyst aligns with Details, when required to perform deep dives and uncover insights. References: Design reports to show details - Training | Microsoft Learn

text: You are optimizing a Power BI report that users say is slow to load. After using Performance Analyzer, you identify that visuals are contributing to the performance issues. Later, you notice that some users still experience slowness even after improvements. Which of the following actions are appropriate steps to take in this situation? (Select all that apply)

options.text: A. Remove unnecessary visuals that don’t add value to the report
options.explanation: Removing unnecessary visuals that do not add value to the report can help reduce the overall load on the report and improve performance by eliminating unnecessary rendering and processing tasks.

options.text: B. Reduce the number of fields used in visuals
options.explanation: Reducing the number of fields used in visuals can help optimize the query performance by minimizing the amount of data being fetched and processed, resulting in faster loading times for the report.

options.text: C. Investigate the semantic model and DAX logic in measures
options.explanation: Investigating the semantic model and DAX logic in measures can help identify any inefficiencies or bottlenecks in the data model and calculations, allowing for optimization to improve report performance.

options.text: D. Rebuild the report using only table visuals
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Rebuilding the report using only table visuals may not necessarily improve performance as the issue may lie in the underlying data model, DAX calculations, or external factors rather than the visual types used in the report.

options.text: E. Meet with the IT department to explore external performance factors
options.explanation: Meeting with the IT department to explore external performance factors such as network latency, server load, or other infrastructure issues can help identify and address any external factors impacting the report's performance.

options.text: F. Add more slicers to improve filtering speed
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Adding more slicers to improve filtering speed may not always lead to improved performance and can potentially add more processing overhead, especially if the slicers are not used efficiently. It is essential to carefully assess the impact of adding more slicers on the report's performance.

explanation: Why correct A. Fewer visuals reduce rendering time and improve load performance. B. Removing non-essential fields from visuals reduces query complexity. C. If visuals aren’t the issue, DAX logic and model design may be the root cause. E. External factors like network or server issues may affect performance for some users. Why others are wrong D. Using only table visuals doesn’t guarantee performance improvement and may reduce report usability. F. Adding more slicers increases complexity and may worsen performance. Keep in Mind: Use Performance Analyzer to identify slow visuals. Remove visuals and fields that don’t add value. Investigate DAX and model design if visuals aren’t the issue. External factors like network and firewalls can affect performance. Collaborate with IT to diagnose user-specific issues. References: Tune report performance - Training | Microsoft Learn

text: You’ve created a Power BI report for a sales team with complex KPIs and calculations. To reduce support requests and make the report self-explanatory, you want to provide visual-specific guidance directly within the report. Which feature should you use?

options.text: B. Use the visual header tooltip icon
options.explanation: Using the visual header tooltip icon allows you to provide detailed explanations, instructions, or additional information directly within the visual itself. This feature can help make the report self-explanatory and reduce the need for external support.

options.text: C. Create a drillthrough page
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Creating a drillthrough page allows users to navigate to a separate page with more detailed information related to a specific data point or visual. While this can enhance the user experience, it may not be the most efficient way to provide visual-specific guidance directly within the report.

options.text: D. Add a filter pane with notes
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Adding a filter pane with notes can help users understand how to interact with the filters in the report, but it may not be the most effective way to provide visual-specific guidance for complex KPIs and calculations within the visuals themselves.

explanation: Why correct The visual header tooltip icon allows you to embed help text or page tooltips directly into a visual’s header, offering contextual guidance without cluttering the report. text: You are designing a Power BI report for a diverse audience. To ensure users can navigate and understand the report without formal training, which of the following techniques should you implement? (Select all that apply)

options.text: A. Add an information page with instructions
options.explanation: Adding an information page with instructions is a helpful technique to guide users on how to navigate and understand the report without the need for formal training. This allows users to quickly grasp the key features and functionalities of the report.

options.text: B. Use bookmarks to create overlays with help text
options.explanation: Using bookmarks to create overlays with help text provides users with contextual information and explanations directly within the report. This interactive feature enhances user understanding and navigation, making it easier for diverse audiences to interpret the data.

options.text: C. Disable all tooltips to simplify visuals
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Disabling all tooltips may hinder users' ability to interact with and understand the visuals in the report. Tooltips often provide additional context and details that can aid users in interpreting the data, especially for those without formal training.

options.text: D. Add a back button to the information page
options.explanation: Adding a back button to the information page allows users to easily navigate back to the previous section or page, improving the overall user experience and making it simpler for diverse audiences to explore the report.

options.text: E. Use the Help icon in visual headers
options.explanation: Using the Help icon in visual headers provides users with quick access to additional information or explanations related to specific visuals in the report. This feature enhances user understanding and allows users to seek help or clarification as needed while navigating the report.

explanation:
Disabling all tooltips may hinder users' ability to interact with and understand the visuals in the report. Tooltips often provide additional context and details that can aid users in interpreting the data, especially for those without formal training.

Visual header tooltip icon

Within the visual header options, you can enable the visual header tooltip. It adds the Help (?) icon to the visual header. Then, you can assign a page tooltip or text. This technique is beneficial for providing visual-specific guidance, such as more detail that describes definitions, calculation logic, or the source of data.

Exam Tips: Do not disable tooltips completely, they help users understand visuals better, especially if they are not trained in reading reports. Tooltips provide extra context, like showing details when you hover over a chart or data point. In the visual header options, you can turn on the tooltip icon (the Help ? symbol). You can link this icon to a page tooltip or custom text. This is useful for giving extra guidance, such as explaining definitions, calculation logic, or the source of data. Practicing with tooltips will help you answer exam questions about how to make reports more userfriendly and accessible.

text: You’re designing a Power BI report for a marketing team and want to make interactive elements more discoverable. What should you configure to achieve this behavior?

options.text: A. Enable action triggers in the button’s bookmark settings
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Enabling action triggers in the button's bookmark settings allows you to define specific actions that should occur when the button is clicked, not when it is hovered over. This configuration is not related to changing the appearance of the button when the user hovers over it.

options.text: B. Apply on-hover formatting to the button’s style properties
options.explanation: Applying on-hover formatting to the button's style properties is the correct choice as it allows you to change the appearance of the button when the user hovers over it. This technique makes interactive elements more discoverable by visually indicating that the button is clickable.

options.text: C. Use a slicer with visual-level filters to simulate interactivity
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Using a slicer with visual-level filters to simulate interactivity is a different approach that does not involve changing the appearance of a button when the user hovers over it. This method is more focused on filtering and displaying specific data in the report.

options.text: D. Add a tooltip to the button with hover text only
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Adding a tooltip to the button with hover text only provides additional information when the user hovers over the button, but it does not change the appearance of the button itself. This technique does not directly address the goal of making clickable buttons more discoverable through visual cues.

explanation: B is correct because on-hover formatting allows you to change the button’s appearance (e.g., color, font, border) when the user hovers over it. This visual feedback like changing text from gray to black, signals that the button is interactive. Why the others are incorrect A. Bookmark actions define what happens when a button is clicked, not how it looks on hover. C. Slicers filter data but don’t simulate button interactivity or hover effects. D. Tooltips provide additional info but don’t visually change the button’s appearance on hover. References: Design reports for navigation - Training | Microsoft Learn

text: You are designing a Power BI report with multiple navigation and interaction buttons. To ensure users can easily discover and use these buttons, which of the following practices should you follow? (Select all that apply)

options.text: A. Place navigation buttons in the same position on every page
options.explanation: Placing navigation buttons in the same position on every page creates consistency and helps users quickly locate and use them without having to search for them. This practice enhances user experience and makes navigation more intuitive.

options.text: B. Use a left-pointing arrow icon for the back button on drillthrough pages
options.explanation: Using a left-pointing arrow icon for the back button on drillthrough pages is a common and recognized symbol for going back. This icon provides a clear visual cue to users about the button's functionality, making it easier for them to understand and use the navigation feature.

options.text: C. Position section-specific buttons near the visuals they affect
options.explanation: Positioning section-specific buttons near the visuals they affect creates a clear relationship between the buttons and the content they interact with. This proximity helps users understand the purpose of the buttons and encourages them to engage with the related visuals, improving the overall usability of the report.

options.text: D. Avoid using tooltips to reduce visual clutter
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Avoiding the use of tooltips to reduce visual clutter is not a recommended practice for ensuring users can easily discover and use navigation buttons. Tooltips can provide additional information and guidance to users, enhancing their understanding of the buttons' functions and improving the overall user experience.

options.text: E. Apply hover effects to make buttons feel interactive
options.explanation: Applying hover effects to make buttons feel interactive is a good practice for enhancing user engagement and providing visual feedback. options.text: F. Randomize button placement to encourage exploration
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Consistency in button placement is key to providing a seamless user experience and ensuring users can easily navigate the report without unnecessary exploration.

explanation: Why these are correct: A. Consistent placement helps users quickly locate navigation buttons across pages. B. A left-pointing arrow is a familiar and intuitive symbol for returning from drillthrough pages. C. Placing buttons near the visuals they control clarifies their purpose. E. options.explanation: Switching between different visual types on the same page using bookmarks is a valid configuration option as it enables users to dynamically change the visualization of data based on their preferences.

options.text: C. Apply bookmarks only through buttons however shapes and images are not supported
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Applying bookmarks only through buttons while shapes and images are not supported is not a valid use case or configuration option for bookmarks in Power BI. Bookmarks can be applied through various interactions, including buttons, shapes, and images.

options.text: D. Capture the current state of slicers and filters
options.explanation: Capturing the current state of slicers and filters using bookmarks is a valid use case as it allows users to save specific filter selections and easily revisit them later.

options.text: E. Control which visuals are affected by the bookmark
options.explanation: Controlling which visuals are affected by the bookmark is a valid configuration option for bookmarks in Power BI. This feature enables users to customize the impact of bookmarks on specific visuals within the report.

options.text: F. Automatically apply bookmarks when a report is opened
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Automatically applying bookmarks when a report is opened is not a valid use case for bookmarks in Power BI. Bookmarks are typically applied manually by users to control the display and interaction of report elements.

explanation: Why correct: A. Bookmarks can reset filters, helping users return to a default view. B. Bookmarks can toggle between visuals (e.g., chart ↔ table) using buttons. D. Bookmarks capture the current state of filters, slicers, and visuals. E. You can configure the scope of visuals affected by a bookmark Why wrong: C. Bookmarks can be triggered by buttons, shapes, and images-not just buttons. F. Bookmarks are not automatically applied when a report opens unless paired with navigation or selection logic. FAQ: 1. What is a bookmark in Power BI? A bookmark captures the current state of a report page including filters, slicers, visual visibility, and page navigation and allows users to return to that exact view with a single click. 2. What can bookmarks be used for? Bookmarks support a wide range of use cases: Resetting filters to default values Switching between visuals (e.g., chart ↔ table) Creating guided navigation experiences Showing/hiding help overlays or instructions Building interactive storytelling dashboards 3. How do I create a bookmark? In Power BI Desktop: Go to the View tab Open the Bookmarks pane Set your desired report state Click Add to create a bookmark Rename and configure it as needed 4. Can bookmarks be triggered by buttons? Yes! You can assign bookmarks to: Buttons Shapes Images This allows users to click and activate bookmarks for navigation or interactivity. 5. What does a bookmark capture? Bookmarks can capture: Visual display state (visible/hidden) Filter and slicer selections Page navigation You can customize what each bookmark includes by adjusting its data, display, and visuals settings. 6. Can bookmarks be used across multiple pages? Yes. Bookmarks can navigate between pages and apply visual states across them, making them ideal for multi-page guided experiences. 7. Do bookmarks update automatically when visuals change? No. Bookmarks capture a snapshot of the report state at the time they’re created. If you change visuals or filters later, you must update the bookmark manually. 8. Can bookmarks be used in published reports? Absolutely. Bookmarks work in both Power BI Desktop and published reports in the Power BI Service. They enhance interactivity for end users. 9. What’s the difference between a bookmark and a tooltip? Bookmark: Captures and restores report state Tooltip: Provides hover-based context or definitions for visuals 10. How do bookmarks improve user experience? They reduce clutter, guide users through complex reports, and make navigation intuitive especially when paired with buttons and overlays. References: Work with bookmarks - Training | Microsoft Learn

text: Left (Bookmark State) Data Display Current Page Right (Description) A. Controls which report page the bookmark navigates to B. Captures slicer selections, sort order, and drill depth C. Manages visibility of visuals, shapes, and other objects

options.text: 1. Data - B 2. Display - C 3. Current Page - A
options.explanation: Choice A is correct because it correctly matches the left (Bookmark State) with the right (Description) in terms of their functionalities. Data captures slicer selections, sort order, and drill depth, Display manages visibility of visuals, shapes, and other objects, and Current Page controls which report page the bookmark navigates to.

options.text: 1. Data - A 2. Display - B 3. Current Page - C
options.explanation: Choice B is incorrect because it mismatches the left (Bookmark State) with the right (Description). It incorrectly associates Data with A, Display with B, and Current Page with C, which does not accurately represent the functionalities of each element in the context of Power BI report design.

explanation:
1. Data - B. Captures slicer selections, sort order, and drill depth

2. Display - C. Manages visibility of visuals, shapes, and other objects

3. Current Page - A. Controls which report page the bookmark navigates to

Keep in Mind:

1. Data - Captures slicer selections, sort order, and drill depth

The Data state records anything that affects the query sent to the semantic model.

This includes:

Slicer/filter selections

Sort order of visuals

Drill level (e.g., hierarchy depth in a matrix or chart)

When you apply a bookmark with Data enabled, it restores these settings exactly as they were when the bookmark was created.

2. Display - Manages visibility of visuals, shapes, and other objects

The Display state controls which objects are visible or hidden.

This includes:

Visuals

Text boxes

Buttons

Shapes and images

You can use the Selection pane to hide/show objects and then capture that state in a bookmark.

This is useful for toggling between views (e.g., chart ↔ table) or showing help overlays.

3. Current Page - Controls which report page the bookmark navigates to

The Current Page state determines whether the bookmark switches to a different report page.

If enabled, clicking the bookmark will take the user to the page that was active when the bookmark was created.

If disabled, the bookmark applies its Data and Display states without changing the page, useful for tooltips or overlays that stay on the same page.

text: You are designing a Power BI report and want to use bookmarks to enhance interactivity and guide users through the report. Which of the following statements about bookmarks are true? (Select all that apply)

options.text: A. Bookmarks can capture slicer selections and sort order
options.explanation: Bookmarks in Power BI can indeed capture slicer selections and sort order, allowing users to save specific views of the data for later reference. Create report bookmarks in Power BI - Power BI | Microsoft Learn Create Page and Bookmark Navigators - Power BI | Microsoft Learn

options.text: B. Bookmarks can be applied only to visuals that were selected when the bookmark was created
options.explanation: Bookmarks are applied to the visuals that were selected when the bookmark was created, allowing users to save and recall specific visualizations within the report.

options.text: C. Bookmarks always navigate to a different report page
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Bookmarks in Power BI do not always navigate to a different report page; they can also be used to navigate within the same page or to show/hide specific visuals.

options.text: D. Bookmarks can toggle visibility of visuals using the Selection pane
options.explanation: Bookmarks can toggle the visibility of visuals using the Selection pane, enabling users to control which visuals are displayed based on their selections.

options.text: E. Bookmarks can be triggered by buttons, shapes, or images
options.explanation: Bookmarks in Power BI can be triggered by buttons, shapes, or images, providing users with interactive elements to navigate through the report. Exam Tips: Create bookmarks while practicing in Power BI. This will help you understand their purpose and how they work. By using bookmarks yourself, you’ll see how they affect visuals, slicers, and navigation. That handson practice makes it easier to answer bookmarkrelated questions in the exam.

options.text: F. Bookmarks automatically update when the report layout changes
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Bookmarks do not automatically update when the report layout changes; users need to manually update them to reflect any changes in the report structure or visuals.

explanation:
Why correct:

A.  Bookmarks capture the Data state, which includes slicer selections, sort order, and drill depth.

B. You can set the scope of a bookmark to affect only Selected visuals, rather than all visuals.

D. The Display state allows bookmarks to toggle visibility of visuals using the Selection pane.

E.  Bookmarks can be triggered by buttons, shapes, or images, making them flexible for user interaction.

Why wrong:

C. Bookmarks can navigate to another page, but they don’t have to. You can disable the Current page state.

F. Bookmarks do not update automatically. You must manually update them if the report layout or filters change.

Keep in Mind:

Bookmarks usually work well, but if you face problems, you may need the visual’s owner to fix or add support.

Any new visual you add after creating a bookmark will show in its default state. The same happens with slicers, they reset to default if added later.

If you move a visual after making a bookmark, the bookmark will remember the new position.

You can change the order of bookmarks, link them to buttons, and even group bookmarks together.

You can decide whether a bookmark should affect all visuals on the page or only specific ones.

6step process to set up a bookmark in Power BI Desktop:

Go to the View tab on the ribbon.

Open the Bookmarks Pane.

Arrange your report page the way you want (apply filters, slicers, hide/show visuals).

In the Bookmarks Pane, click Add to create a new bookmark.

Rename the bookmark to something meaningful (like “Top Sales View”).

Use the bookmark by selecting it, or assign it to a button for easy navigation.

text: Scenario: Ramesh wants to create a bookmark in Power BI that resets slicers but does not change other visuals on the page. To achieve this, he should configure the bookmark with the __________ scope and enable the __________ state. Options for Blank 1: A. All visuals B. Selected visuals C. Entire report D. Current page Options for Blank 2: A. Display B. Data C. Current view D. Format

options.text: Selected visuals, Data
options.explanation: Configuring the bookmark with the "Selected visuals" scope ensures that only the specific visuals with slicers are affected when the bookmark is applied. Enabling the "Data" state ensures that the slicers are reset to their default state without affecting the visualizations or other data in the report.

options.text: All visuals, Display
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Choosing the "All visuals" scope would reset all visuals in the report, not just the slicers, which is not the desired outcome when resetting slicers. Additionally, the "Display" state does not specifically target the slicers or their data, so it would not achieve the goal of resetting slicers without affecting other visuals.

options.text: Current page, Data
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Setting the bookmark with the "Current page" scope would only affect the visuals on the current page, not specifically targeting the slicers for reset. Additionally, the "Data" state is necessary to ensure that the slicers are reset to their default state, which is not achieved with the "Current page" scope.

explanation: Keep in Mind: All visuals applies the bookmark to every object on the page, which may unintentionally affect other visuals like charts or drill states. Display controls visibility (hide/show), not slicer values. Current page determines navigation, not slicer behavior. While Data is correct for capturing slicer values, pairing it with Current page doesn’t help isolate slicers or prevent impact on other visuals. References: Work with bookmarks - Training | Microsoft Learn

text: You want users to toggle between a bar chart and a map on the same report page. What is the best approach?

options.text: A. Use slicers to filter between chart and map
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Using slicers to filter between the chart and map visuals would allow users to switch between them, but it may not provide a seamless and intuitive experience for toggling between the two visuals on the same page.

options.text: B. Create separate pages for each visual
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Creating separate pages for each visual would require users to navigate between different pages to view the desired visual, which may not be the most efficient way to toggle between a bar chart and a map on the same report page.

options.text: C. Use buttons linked to bookmarks that toggle visibility
options.explanation: Using buttons linked to bookmarks that toggle visibility is the best approach as it allows users to easily switch between the bar chart and map on the same report page with a simple click. This method provides a more user-friendly and interactive experience for toggling between visuals.

options.text: D. Use tooltips to describe each visual
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Using tooltips to describe each visual is not the best approach for toggling between a bar chart and a map on the same report page. Tooltips are typically used for providing additional information about a specific data point within a visual, rather than toggling between different visuals on the same page.

explanation: Swapping visuals like toggling between a bar chart and a map is best achieved by using bookmarks that capture the Display state (which visuals are shown or hidden) and assigning those bookmarks to buttons. This allows users to stay on the same report page and interactively switch between views. You create two visuals (e.g., a bar chart and a map) on the same page. Use the Selection pane to control which visual is visible. Create a bookmark for each state (e.g., one with the bar chart visible, one with the map). Add buttons labeled “Chart” and “Map” and assign each to the corresponding bookmark. This method is clean, intuitive, and keeps the user experience seamless. References: Work with bookmarks - Training | Microsoft Learn

text: You are creating a Power BI dataset for Contoso Ltd. and need to identify the correct sequence of steps. Which of the following options correctly arranges the steps to swap visuals using bookmarks in Power BI?

options.text: Assign bookmarks to buttons Update bookmarks with visual visibility states Configure bookmarks to capture Display state only Set scope to Selected visuals
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. This arrangement does not follow the correct steps to swap visuals using bookmarks in Power BI. Assigning bookmarks to buttons should come after configuring bookmarks to capture Display state only and updating bookmarks with visual visibility states. Setting the scope to Selected visuals should be done before assigning bookmarks to buttons.

options.text: Configure bookmarks to capture Display state only Set scope to Selected visuals Update bookmarks with one visual shown and one hidden Assign bookmarks to buttons
options.explanation: This is the correct arrangement of steps to swap visuals using bookmarks in Power BI. First, configure bookmarks to capture Display state only. Then, set the scope to Selected visuals. Next, update bookmarks with one visual shown and one hidden. Finally, assign bookmarks to buttons to enable swapping between visuals.

options.text: Set scope to All visuals Update bookmarks with both visuals visible Assign bookmarks to buttons Enable Data and Display states
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. This arrangement does not correctly arrange the steps to swap visuals using bookmarks in Power BI. Setting the scope to All visuals is not necessary for swapping visuals. Updating bookmarks with both visuals visible should come after configuring bookmarks to capture Display state only. Enabling Data and Display states is not required for swapping visuals.

options.text: Create separate pages for each visual Use slicers to toggle visibility Assign slicers to bookmarks Enable Current page state
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. This arrangement does not correctly arrange the steps to swap visuals using bookmarks in Power BI. Creating separate pages for each visual and using slicers to toggle visibility is not the most efficient way to swap visuals using bookmarks. Assigning slicers to bookmarks and enabling Current page state are not necessary steps for swapping visuals using bookmarks.

explanation: Phrase from Learning Path: Swapping a visual requires two bookmarks, and you can do so by following these steps: Configure each bookmark to capture the Display state but not the Data state. These settings preserve any sorting or other filtering. Configure each bookmark to use the Selected visuals scope, targeting the initially visible visual and the hidden visual. Update the first bookmark, with one visual as visible and the other as hidden. Update the second bookmark by using the inverse visibility state. Assign the bookmarks to button actions. References: Work with bookmarks - Training | Microsoft Learn
