text: Which of the following best describes the primary distinction between Power BI Desktop and the Power BI service in a typical workflow?

options.text: A. Power BI Desktop is used for consuming reports, while the Power BI service is used for authoring them.
options.explanation: Power BI Desktop is actually used for creating and authoring reports, not just consuming them. The Power BI service is where reports are shared, published, and interacted with by users.

options.text: B. Power BI Desktop is a SaaS platform, while the Power BI service is a client application.
options.explanation: Power BI Desktop is a client application that is installed on a user's machine, while the Power BI service is a cloud-based platform accessed through a web browser. They serve different purposes in the Power BI workflow.

options.text: C. Power BI Desktop is primarily for building and authoring reports, while the Power BI service is for publishing, sharing, and interacting with them.
options.explanation: Power BI Desktop is designed for building and authoring reports locally on a user's machine, while the Power BI service is used for sharing, publishing, and interacting with those reports in a collaborative online environment.

options.text: D. Both Power BI Desktop and the Power BI service are used interchangeably for authoring and sharing reports.
options.explanation: Power BI Desktop and the Power BI service have distinct roles in the Power BI workflow. While both can be used for authoring reports, Power BI Desktop is primarily for report creation, whereas the Power BI service is focused on sharing and interacting with those reports.

explanation:
Power BI Desktop This is an application you install on your computer. It is mainly used for creating reports. You can connect to different data sources, clean and shape the data, and then design visuals like charts and tables. Everything you do here is local, meaning it stays on your machine until you decide to share it. Think of Power BI Desktop as your personal workshop where you build and design reports.

Power BI Service This is the online platform (cloud-based) where reports and dashboards are shared with others. After you finish building a report in Power BI Desktop, you publish it to the Power BI Service. In the service, people can view, interact with, and collaborate on the reports. They can filter data, drill down into details, and leave feedback. The service also allows you to manage permissions, schedule data refreshes, and organize content into workspaces for teams. Think of Power BI Service as the shared office space where everyone can access and work with the reports you created.

In short:

Power BI Desktop = build and design reports locally.

Power BI Service = share, publish, and collaborate online.

Keep in Mind:

Power BI Service supports scheduled refresh, DirectQuery, and streaming datasets to keep reports up to date.

It enhances collaboration by allowing multiple users to work together on the same dataset.

Power BI Desktop is best for building individual reports locally, while the Service supports teamwork online.

Workspaces act as collaborative hubs where teams share and manage assets such as dashboards, reports, models, and workbooks.

Workspaces can be organized based on company structure, specific projects, or report versions.

Roles within workspaces define permissions, controlling who can edit, share, or only view content.

This role-based system makes collaboration smoother and keeps data secure.

text: Neha, a data analyst at PRQ Corporation, notices that her workspace performance is slow due to large datasets and frequent refreshes. Her manager suggests moving the workspace to Premium capacity. What benefit will Neha gain?

options.text: A. Unlimited storage for datasets
options.explanation: Moving the workspace to Premium capacity does not provide unlimited storage for datasets. While Premium capacity offers enhanced performance and capabilities, there are still limitations on storage based on the selected Premium SKU.

options.text: B. Higher refresh rates and dedicated resources for performance
options.explanation: By moving the workspace to Premium capacity, Neha will benefit from higher refresh rates and dedicated resources for performance. Premium capacity offers more processing power and resources, which can significantly improve the workspace's performance with large datasets and frequent refreshes. Power BI Premium FAQ - Microsoft Fabric | Microsoft Learn Check the description for comparison between Pro and Premium license. Along with Roles, questions will come around licenses as well.

options.text: C. Ability to bypass row-level security
options.explanation: Premium capacity does not provide the ability to bypass row-level security. Row-level security settings are independent of the workspace's capacity type and are managed within Power BI itself.

options.text: D. Automatic conversion of reports into dashboards
options.explanation: Premium capacity does not automatically convert reports into dashboards. While Premium capacity offers additional features and capabilities, the conversion of reports into dashboards is a manual process that needs to be done within the Power BI service.

explanation: When Neha moves her workspace to Premium capacity, the reports and datasets in that workspace will run faster and more smoothly. Premium capacity gives extra computing power and memory compared to the standard setup. This means large datasets can be handled better, and scheduled data refreshes can happen more often without slowing things down. Premium also ensures dedicated resources, so performance is not affected by other users outside the workspace. Overall, Premium capacity makes collaboration easier and more reliable when dealing with heavy data loads or frequent updates. text: Suresh, at Tech Company, wants to share a workspace with external clients. Which of the following conditions must be met?

options.text: A. External sharing is only possible through "My Workspace"
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. External sharing in Power BI is not limited to "My Workspace" only. Workspaces can be shared with external users through various methods, not just "My Workspace".

options.text: B. External users must have a Power BI Pro license or the workspace must be in Premium capacity
options.explanation: External users must have a Power BI Pro license, or the workspace must be in Premium capacity to access shared workspaces. This ensures that external users have the necessary permissions and capabilities to view and interact with the shared content. Knowledge Base: If you want to know what license is assigned to you, you can refer this guide. Licenses and Subscriptions for Business Users - Power BI | Microsoft Learn

options.text: C. External users can access without any license requirements
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. External users cannot access shared workspaces without any license requirements. Power BI Pro license or Premium capacity is needed for external users to access shared workspaces and their content.

options.text: D. External sharing is restricted to semantic models only
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. External sharing in Power BI is not restricted to semantic models only. Workspaces, reports, dashboards, and other content can be shared with external users, not limited to semantic models.

explanation: As a power bi user, you need to know the pricing of different license. Power BI: Pricing Plan | Microsoft Power Platform Keep in Mind: Know how to convert a workspace into premium workspace: If you already have a regular Pro workspace with reports and dashboards, you can upgrade it without needing to republish anything. The process is quick and straightforward. Open Workspace Settings Go to the workspace you want to upgrade. Click the three dots (…) next to its name and choose Workspace settings. Select the Premium Tab In the settings window, open the Premium tab. Turn On Premium Capacity Switch the Premium Capacity option to On. Then pick the right capacity from the dropdown list, just like when setting up a new workspace. Save Changes Click Save. The upgrade takes effect immediately. All the content in that workspace will now use Premium capacity, and you’ll see a diamond icon next to the workspace name. References: How to Create a Premium Workspace in Power BI

text: Ravi, a report designer at Infosys, publishes a report to the Finance workspace. His colleague Priya opens the report in her browser and wants to create a new report using the same dataset. Which statement correctly explains how Priya can achieve this?

options.text: A. Priya must request Ravi to export the dataset from Power BI Desktop.
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Exporting the dataset from Power BI Desktop is not necessary for Priya to create a new report using the same dataset. The dataset is already available in the Finance workspace, and Priya can directly access and use it for creating a new report without involving Ravi in the process.

options.text: B. Priya can build a new report directly in the workspace using the semantic model created when Ravi published.
options.explanation: When Ravi published the report to the Finance workspace, the semantic model (dataset) associated with the report is also published. Priya can utilize this semantic model to build a new report directly in the workspace without the need to export or download any files from Power BI Desktop. Exercise - Configure a semantic model in Power BI Desktop - Training | Microsoft Learn Semantic Models in the Power BI Service - Power BI | Microsoft Learn

options.text: C. Priya can only duplicate Ravi’s report; she cannot create a new one.
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Priya is not limited to duplicating Ravi's report. She has the flexibility to create a new report using the same dataset that Ravi published to the Finance workspace. This allows Priya to customize and design her own report based on the existing dataset.

options.text: D. Priya must download the report as a .pbix file and re-upload it.
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Downloading the report as a .pbix file and re-uploading it is not necessary for Priya to create a new report. The dataset is already available in the workspace, and Priya can leverage it to build a new report without the need to handle .pbix files.

explanation: When Ravi publishes a report to the Finance workspace, Power BI automatically publishes the semantic model (dataset) along with it. That dataset becomes available in the workspace. Priya, who has access to the workspace, can then: Open the workspace in the Power BI service. Select New report. Choose the existing semantic model (the one created when Ravi published his report). Build her own visuals and layout using that shared dataset. This works because in Power BI, reports and datasets are separate but linked artifacts. Publishing a report always creates or connects to a dataset (semantic model), and other users with permission can reuse that dataset to build new reports without duplicating data connections. Semantic Models in the Power BI Service - Power BI | Microsoft Learn

section: Design effective reports in Power BI
text: Ravi, a BI developer at ABC Corporation, publishes a report from Power BI Desktop to the Finance workspace. His colleague Priya notices that a semantic model is created along with the report. What does this semantic model contain?

options.text: A. A collection of visuals and slicers embedded in the report pages
options.explanation: This choice is incorrect as a semantic model in Power BI contains more than just visuals and slicers. It includes the underlying data structure and logic that defines the dataset.

options.text: B. Tables, relationships, and measures defining the structure and logic of the dataset
options.explanation: This choice is correct because a semantic model in Power BI consists of tables, relationships, and measures that define the structure and logic of the dataset. This model is essential for data analysis and visualization within Power BI reports.

options.text: C. Metadata about workspace roles and user permissions
options.explanation: This choice is incorrect as the semantic model in Power BI does not contain metadata about workspace roles and user permissions. These aspects are related to security and access control within the workspace, not the data model itself.

options.text: D. A snapshot of the data at the time of publishing, without refresh capability
options.explanation: This choice is incorrect as the semantic model in Power BI does not consist of a snapshot of the data at the time of publishing. Instead, it contains the underlying structure and relationships that define the dataset for analysis and reporting.

explanation:
When Ravi publishes a report from Power BI Desktop to the Finance workspace, Power BI automatically creates a semantic model (dataset) alongside the report. This semantic model is the foundation of the report and contains:

Tables: The structured data imported or connected from the source systems.

Relationships: The defined links between tables (e.g., onetomany, manytoone) that enable crosstable analysis.

Measures: DAX calculations that define business logic, aggregations, KPIs, and other analytical expressions.

In short, the semantic model is what gives the report its data structure and analytical logic, allowing Priya (or any colleague with access) to build new reports on top of the same dataset without duplicating the data connection.

section: Design effective reports in Power BI
text: At KYC Bank, Arjun is searching for datasets to build a new compliance report. He uses the Data hub in the Power BI service. What does this feature allow him to do?

options.text: A. Browse only semantic models created in his personal workspace
options.explanation: The Data hub in the Power BI service enables Arjun to access a wide range of semantic models beyond those specifically created in his personal workspace. This feature allows him to discover datasets from various sources and locations within the organization, enhancing the options available for his compliance report.

options.text: B. Browse semantic models available to him across workspaces, regardless of their location
options.explanation: By utilizing the Data hub in the Power BI service, Arjun gains the ability to browse through semantic models from different workspaces, providing him with a comprehensive view of available datasets. This functionality allows him to leverage data from diverse sources and collaborate effectively across different projects.

options.text: C. Browse only certified semantic models approved by administrators
options.explanation: The Data hub in the Power BI service does not limit Arjun to only certified semantic models approved by administrators. Instead, it empowers him to discover semantic models across workspaces, giving him the freedom to choose datasets that best suit his compliance reporting needs, regardless of certification status.

options.text: D. Browse dashboards and apps but not semantic models directly
options.explanation: Through the Data hub in the Power BI service, Arjun is not restricted to browsing dashboards and apps exclusively. This feature specifically focuses on enabling users to discover and access semantic models, allowing Arjun to delve into the underlying data structures and relationships to gather insights for his compliance report.

explanation: In the Power BI service, the Data hub is designed to help users like Arjun quickly discover and reuse existing semantic models (datasets). When Ravi or any other colleague publishes a report, the associated semantic model becomes available through the Data hub. Through the Data hub: Arjun can see semantic models available to him (for which he has Build permission), not just those in his current workspace. It allows him to search across workspaces he has access to, regardless of their location. This makes it easier to reuse existing datasets instead of duplicating data connections or rebuilding models. He can then build his new compliance report directly on top of one of these shared semantic models. In short, the Data hub is a cross-workspace discovery tool for semantic models, enabling collaboration and consistency in reporting. Create reports based on semantic models from different workspaces - Power BI | Microsoft Learn

text: Neha, a manager at ABC Corporation, wants to ensure her team uses the correct dataset for building reports. She asks the BI team to promote a semantic model. What is the difference between promotion and certification?

options.text: A. Promotion increases visibility within the organization, while certification indicates formal endorsement and trustworthiness
options.explanation: Promotion increases visibility within the organization by making the dataset more accessible and discoverable to users. Certification, on the other hand, indicates formal endorsement and trustworthiness of the dataset, ensuring that it meets specific standards and criteria for reliability and accuracy. Promote and Certify Power BI Content with Endorsement - Power BI | Microsoft Learn

options.text: B. Promotion automatically applies incremental refresh, while certification applies scheduled refresh
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Promotion and certification are not directly related to the refresh mechanisms of datasets. While promotion focuses on increasing visibility and accessibility, certification emphasizes formal endorsement and trustworthiness of the dataset.

options.text: C. Promotion is restricted to Premium capacity workspaces, while certification is available in Pro workspaces
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Promotion and certification are not limited to specific workspace capacities. Promotion aims to increase visibility and accessibility of the dataset, while certification focuses on endorsing the dataset's trustworthiness and reliability.

options.text: D. Promotion converts semantic models into apps, while certification converts them into dashboards
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Promotion and certification do not involve converting semantic models into apps or dashboards. Promotion is about increasing visibility and accessibility, while certification is about endorsing the trustworthiness and reliability of the dataset.

explanation:
Promotion is about visibility and awareness. When something is promoted (like a report, dataset, or feature in Power BI), it becomes easier for colleagues across the organization to discover and use it. It’s essentially about making it known and accessible.

Certification goes a step further. It’s a formal endorsement that signals the dataset or report has been vetted, is trustworthy, and can be relied upon for official decisionmaking. Certification is about quality assurance and governance, not just visibility.

In short:

Promotion = discoverability

Certification = credibility

section: Design effective reports in Power BI
text: Ravi, a BI developer at Infosys, has created multiple dashboards and reports in a workspace. His manager Priya wants the entire HR department to access them without managing workspace permissions for each user. What should Ravi do?

options.text: A. Share each dashboard individually with all HR employees
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Sharing each dashboard individually with all HR employees would create a maintenance nightmare for Ravi. It would require constant updates and changes to permissions for each user, leading to potential errors and security risks.

options.text: B. Export the reports to Excel and email them to the department
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Exporting the reports to Excel and emailing them to the department is not a scalable solution. It lacks interactivity, real-time data updates, and the ability to drill down into details that Power BI offers. It also poses a risk of data leakage through email.

options.text: C. Package the dashboards and reports into a Power BI app and share it with the HR department
options.explanation: Packaging the dashboards and reports into a Power BI app and sharing it with the HR department is the most efficient and secure method. Power BI apps provide a centralized platform for accessing multiple reports and dashboards, ensuring consistent data access and security controls for all users. Power BI Workspace vs App: Build in One and Share ... - Microsoft Fabric Community

options.text: D. Grant all HR employees Contributor access to the workspace
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Granting all HR employees Contributor access to the workspace is not advisable as it gives them unnecessary permissions to edit, delete, or publish content within the workspace. This can lead to accidental changes or unauthorized access to sensitive information.

explanation:
In Power BI, when Ravi has created multiple dashboards and reports in a workspace, the most efficient way to share them with a large audience (like the entire HR department) is to package them into a Power BI app.

Here’s why this works:

Apps simplify distribution: Instead of assigning workspace permissions to each HR user individually, Ravi can publish an app from the workspace.

Centralized access: The app bundles all dashboards and reports together, so Priya and the HR team see a single, organized entry point.

Controlled permissions: Ravi can manage access at the app level, granting the HR department visibility without giving them edit rights to the workspace.

Governance & consistency: Apps ensure that users consume the official version of reports, reducing duplication or accidental edits.

In short:

Workspace = development & collaboration

App = distribution to a broad audience

section: Design effective reports in Power BI
text: Suresh, at ABC Corporation designs an app for the Sales department. He wants to release updates only when he decides, rather than having changes appear immediately. Which feature of apps allows him to do this?

options.text: A. Version control in Power BI Desktop
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Version control in Power BI Desktop allows users to manage different versions of their reports and datasets within the Power BI Desktop application. It does not control the release of updates to end-users or determine when changes appear.

options.text: B. Scheduled refresh in the semantic model
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Scheduled refresh in the semantic model is a feature that allows users to automatically refresh data in their Power BI reports at specified intervals. It is not related to controlling the release of app updates or determining when changes appear to end-users.

options.text: C. Control over publishing new app versions
options.explanation: Control over publishing new app versions in Power BI allows users to manage the release of updates to their apps. This feature gives users the ability to decide when changes are made available to end-users, ensuring that updates are released only when desired.

explanation:
In Power BI, when you design an app in a workspace, you can keep making changes to reports, dashboards, and datasets inside that workspace. However, those changes are not automatically visible to end users of the app. Instead:

You can edit and refine content in the workspace as much as you want.

Users of the app continue to see the last published version until you explicitly publish a new one.

This gives you full control over when updates are released, ensuring that changes are only rolled out when they’re ready and approved.

In short:

Workspace = development area (changes are ongoing).

App = controlled distribution (users only see updates when a new version is published).

section: Design effective reports in Power BI
text: At ABC Corporation Bank, Arjun wants to share dashboards with two different audiences: senior management and branch managers. Both groups should see the same app but with tailored content. Which approach should he use?

options.text: A. Create separate workspaces for each audience
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Creating separate workspaces for each audience would require duplicating the dashboards and managing multiple versions of the same content, which can lead to inconsistencies and maintenance challenges. It is not the most efficient approach for sharing tailored content with different audiences.

options.text: B. Create one app and configure audience targeting within it
options.explanation: Creating one app and configuring audience targeting within it allows Arjun to share the same app with both senior management and branch managers, while customizing the content each audience sees. This approach ensures consistency, simplifies management, and provides a tailored experience for each group.

options.text: C. Duplicate dashboards and share them individually
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Duplicating dashboards and sharing them individually can lead to duplication of effort, inconsistencies in content, and difficulties in managing updates across multiple versions. It is not the most efficient way to share tailored content with different audiences.

options.text: D. Use row-level security in the semantic model instead of apps
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Using row-level security in the semantic model instead of apps may limit the ability to customize the content for different audiences within the same app. It is more suitable for restricting access to specific data based on user roles or permissions, rather than tailoring the content of the app for different audiences.

explanation:
In Power BI, audience targeting within apps allows you to publish a single app but configure different views of content for different groups of users. Here’s how it works for Arjun’s scenario at ABC Corporation Bank:

One app, multiple audiences: Arjun creates a single app from the workspace.

Audience targeting: He defines audiences such as Senior Management and Branch Managers.

Tailored content: Each audience sees only the dashboards and reports relevant to them, even though they’re accessing the same app.

Simplified governance: This avoids duplicating apps or managing separate workspaces, while still ensuring each group gets the right content.

In short: One app + audience targeting = personalized content delivery.

section: Design effective reports in Power BI
text: Neha, a manager at ABC Corporation, asks her team to explain why workspaces are considered containers in Power BI. Which explanation is correct?

options.text: A. Shared workspace allows multiple users to collaborate with role-based access control on reports, dashboards, and datasets.
options.explanation: Shared workspaces in Power BI act as containers because they allow multiple users to collaborate on reports, dashboards, and datasets within a secure environment. Role-based access control ensures that each user has the appropriate permissions to view and edit the content within the workspace.

options.text: B. Shared workspace is private to an individual user and cannot be accessed by others.
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Shared workspaces being private to an individual user and inaccessible to others does not align with the concept of workspaces as containers in Power BI. Workspaces are designed to facilitate collaboration and sharing among team members, rather than restricting access to a single user.

options.text: C. Shared workspace automatically converts all reports into dashboards for easier monitoring.
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. While shared workspaces in Power BI may automatically convert reports into dashboards for easier monitoring, this functionality does not directly relate to why workspaces are considered containers. The primary purpose of workspaces as containers is to provide a centralized location for storing and managing Power BI content.

options.text: D. Shared workspace eliminates the need for semantic models by storing only visuals.
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Shared workspaces in Power BI do not eliminate the need for semantic models or only store visuals. Workspaces serve as containers for organizing and managing reports, dashboards, datasets, and other Power BI artifacts, allowing users to work collaboratively on creating and sharing insights.

explanation:
In Power BI, workspaces are considered containers because they serve as the central place where all related content (reports, dashboards, datasets, and dataflows) is stored and managed together. Here’s why the statement is accurate:

Collaboration hub: A shared workspace allows multiple users to work together on the same set of Power BI assets.

Role-based access control: Permissions can be assigned (Admin, Member, Contributor, Viewer), ensuring that each user has the right level of access.

Unified container: Reports, dashboards, datasets, and dataflows are all organized within the workspace, making it easier to manage and govern.

Separation of development and distribution: Workspaces are used for building and collaboration, while apps (published from workspaces) are used for distribution to larger audiences.

In short: Workspaces = containers for collaboration + governance of Power BI content.

text: When creating a new Power BI workspace, which of the following inputs can you provide? (Select all that apply)

options.text: A. A unique name for the workspace
options.explanation: Providing a unique name for the workspace is essential when creating a new Power BI workspace to easily identify and differentiate it from other workspaces within the organization.

options.text: B. An optional description to explain the purpose of the workspace
options.explanation: Adding an optional description helps to clarify the purpose and scope of the workspace, making it easier for team members to understand its intended use and objectives.

options.text: C. A workspace image uploaded as a .png or .jpg file
options.explanation: Uploading a workspace image in .png or .jpg format allows for customization and personalization of the workspace, making it visually appealing and easily recognizable.

options.text: D. A contact list to identify responsible people
options.explanation: Including a contact list helps to identify responsible individuals or teams who are accountable for managing and maintaining the workspace, facilitating effective communication and collaboration.

options.text: E. A mandatory dataset to initialize the workspace
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. A mandatory dataset is not required to initialize the workspace. While datasets are essential for data analysis and visualization in Power BI, they are not a prerequisite for creating a new workspace.

options.text: F. A default dashboard that must be created before saving
options.explanation: Creating a default dashboard before saving the workspace is not necessary. Dashboards can be added and customized after the workspace is created, based on the specific reporting and visualization needs of the users.

explanation: A: Name is required and must be unique. B: Description is optional but helps others understand the purpose. C: You can upload an image (.png or .jpg) to visually identify the workspace. D: Contact list identifies who is responsible for the workspace. E: Wrong - datasets are added later, not required at creation. F: Wrong - dashboards are not mandatory when creating a workspace.

section: Design effective reports in Power BI
text: You have created a detailed sales performance report in Power BI Desktop that needs to be reviewed by multiple teams across your organization. However: The report file size is too large to send via email. Some colleagues are using older versions of Power BI Desktop, causing compatibility issues. You also need to ensure that everyone is always looking at the latest version of the report without confusion. In this situation, what is the best way to share the report with your colleagues so they can access it online, collaborate seamlessly, and avoid versioning or compatibility problems?

options.text: Send the .pbix file via email to all colleagues.
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Sending the .pbix file via email is not the best option as the file size may be too large to send, causing issues with email delivery. Additionally, colleagues using older versions of Power BI Desktop may face compatibility problems when trying to open the file.

options.text: Save the report as a PDF and share it through a shared drive.
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Saving the report as a PDF and sharing it through a shared drive may help with file size issues, but it does not provide the interactive features and real-time data updates that Power BI offers. Colleagues will not be able to interact with the data or access the latest information.

options.text: Publish the report to the Power BI service so colleagues can access it online.
options.explanation: Publishing the report to the Power BI service is the best option in this situation. It allows colleagues to access the report online, collaborate seamlessly, and ensures that everyone is looking at the latest version of the report without compatibility issues. The Power BI service also provides real-time data updates and interactive features for a better user experience.

options.text: Ask each colleague to install the latest version of Power BI Desktop and open the file individually.
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Asking each colleague to install the latest version of Power BI Desktop and open the file individually is not a practical solution. It may be time-consuming and lead to confusion, especially if there are multiple versions of the report circulating among colleagues. Publishing the report to the Power BI service is a more efficient way to ensure everyone has access to the latest version without compatibility issues.

explanation: Large file size: No need to send the .pbix file via email. Once published, the report is hosted in the cloud. Compatibility problems: Colleagues don’t need to worry about which version of Power BI Desktop they’re using. They can simply open the report in their browser via the Power BI service. Always up to date: Everyone accessing the report online will see the latest version. You control updates by republishing or refreshing the dataset. Collaboration: Multiple teams can view, interact with, and even build new reports off the same semantic model (dataset) without duplicating files. Governance: You can manage access through workspace roles or publish the report as part of a Power BI app for broader distribution. In short: Publishing to the Power BI service centralizes access, eliminates version confusion, and ensures seamless collaboration across teams. References: Publish to Power BI service - Training | Microsoft Learn

text: Ravi wants to create a workspace for his small analytics team at Infosys. They need to collaborate but don’t require advanced features like AI or large semantic models. Which license mode should he choose?

options.text: A. Premium Per User (PPU)
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Premium Per User (PPU) licenses are designed for individual users who require advanced features like AI capabilities and large semantic models. Since Ravi's team does not need these advanced features, choosing PPU licenses would be unnecessary and more costly.

options.text: B. Fabric Capacity
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Fabric Capacity licenses are used for organizations that require dedicated capacity for their Power BI workloads. Since Ravi's team is small and does not need advanced features, opting for Fabric Capacity licenses would be excessive and not cost-effective.

options.text: C. Power BI Pro
options.explanation: Power BI Pro licenses are suitable for teams that need to collaborate and share reports and dashboards. These licenses provide the necessary features for collaboration without the additional cost of advanced features like AI or large semantic models, making them the ideal choice for Ravi's small analytics team at Infosys.

options.text: D. Free Workspace
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Free Workspace does not require any licenses and provides basic collaboration features. However, it may not offer the necessary functionality for a small analytics team like Ravi's at Infosys, as it lacks some advanced features that could enhance their workflow.

explanation:
Collaboration needs: Power BI Pro licenses allow users to create workspaces where multiple team members can collaborate on reports, dashboards, and datasets.

No advanced requirements: Since Ravi’s team doesn’t need premium features like AI capabilities, large semantic models, or dedicated capacity, Pro is sufficient.

Cost-effective: Power BI Pro is the most economical way for small teams to share and collaborate without requiring Premium capacity.

Access control: With Pro, Ravi can manage workspace roles (Admin, Member, Contributor, Viewer) to ensure proper governance.

In short: Power BI Pro = best fit for small teams who need collaboration but don’t require enterprise-scale Premium features.

explanation:

This is incorrect option. Power BI Pro is primarily for collaboration for small teams, where all users need a Pro license. Premium Per User (PPU) includes Pro features along with AI capabilities, larger models, and more data refreshes. explanation: A Power BI Pro license allows users to create workspaces and share content, but all users who access the workspace must also have a Pro license. It's ideal for individuals or teams needing Premium features without committing to full Fabric Capacity. section: Design effective reports in Power BI
text: You have created a report in Power BI Desktop and choose File > Publish > Publish to Power BI. After signing in with your Microsoft Entra ID and completing the publish process, which of the following outcomes are correct? (Select all that apply)

options.text: The report is published to the selected workspace in the Power BI Service.
options.explanation: When you publish a report to Power BI using the Publish to Power BI feature in Power BI Desktop, the report is uploaded and stored in the specified workspace within the Power BI Service, making it accessible to authorized users.

options.text: The semantic model (tables, relationships, measures) is also published and can be reused to build new reports or dashboards.
options.explanation: In addition to the report itself, the semantic model that includes tables, relationships, and measures is also uploaded and published along with the report. This semantic model can be leveraged to create new reports or dashboards based on the same data.

options.text: You receive a link to the published report for easy access and sharing.
options.explanation: Upon successful completion of the publish process, you will receive a link to the published report. This link enables easy access to the report and facilitates sharing it with others within your organization.

options.text: Republishing a modified report may replace the existing semantic model and impact connected reports or dashboards.
options.explanation: Modifying and republishing a report in Power BI may result in the replacement of the existing semantic model. This replacement can potentially impact any connected reports or dashboards that rely on the previous version of the model.

options.text: The report is automatically emailed to all workspace members without any further action.
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. The report is not automatically emailed to all workspace members after publishing. Sharing the report via email or other communication channels needs to be done manually to ensure that the intended recipients have access to the report.

options.text: Republishing prevents further scheduled refreshes from running until you manually reconfigure them.
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Republishing a report in Power BI does not inherently halt or prevent scheduled refreshes from running. The scheduled refresh settings remain intact unless manually adjusted or reconfigured to accommodate any changes made during the republishing process.

explanation: Lines from Learning Path: Publish from Power BI Desktop In Power BI Desktop, choose File > Publish > Publish to Power BI or select Publish on the Home ribbon. If you aren't signed in yet with your Microsoft Entra ID (work or school account), you're prompted to do so. After signing in, you'll see a dialog box that allows you to select the workspace where you want to publish the report. When publishing is complete, you receive a link to your report. You can also find the report in the Power BI service by navigating to the workspace you selected during the publish process. Notice the semantic model is also published with the report. This means that the data model, including tables, relationships, and measures, is now available in the Power BI service. You can use this semantic model to create new reports or dashboards based on the same data. When you make a change to a report in Power BI Desktop and then republish it, a message shows you how many workspaces, reports, and dashboards are potentially impacted by the change. Power BI then asks you to confirm that you want to replace the currently published semantic model with the one you modified. References: Publish to Power BI service - Training | Microsoft Learn Publish from Power BI Desktop - Power BI | Microsoft Learn

section: Design effective reports in Power BI
text: Which of the following statements about uploading a Power BI report (.pbix file) to a workspace is correct?

options.text: Uploading a report is only possible from Power BI Desktop using the Publish option.
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Uploading a report to a workspace can be done not only from Power BI Desktop but also directly in the Power BI Service using the Import or Browse menu. This allows users to upload .pbix files without the need to go through Power BI Desktop first.

options.text: You can upload a .pbix file directly to a workspace using the Import or Browse menu in the Power BI Service.
options.explanation: You can upload a .pbix file directly into a workspace in the Power BI Service using the Import or Browse option, without needing to publish from Power BI Desktop first. This creates the report and its associated semantic model in that workspace.

options.text: If you connect to a file stored in OneDrive for work or school or SharePoint, Power BI can automatically sync changes approximately every hour.
options.explanation: When connecting to a file stored in OneDrive for work or school or SharePoint, Power BI has the capability to automatically sync changes approximately every hour. This feature ensures that the reports in the workspace are kept up to date with any modifications made to the original file.

options.text: Once uploaded, reports cannot be updated or synced with changes made in the original file.
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Reports uploaded to a workspace can be updated and synced with changes made in the original file. This feature enables users to make modifications to the report in Power BI Desktop and have those changes reflected in the workspace, ensuring data accuracy and consistency.

explanation: Direct Upload You can upload a .pbix file directly into a workspace in the Power BI Service using the Import or Browse option. This publishes the report and creates the associated semantic model (dataset) in that workspace. OneDrive/SharePoint Sync If the .pbix file is stored in OneDrive for work or school or SharePoint Online, Power BI can connect to it. Power BI will then automatically sync changes approximately every hour, ensuring the online version stays updated with the source file. This avoids version confusion and keeps the workspace report aligned with the latest edits made in Desktop. In short: Upload directly = manual publish. OneDrive/SharePoint connection = automatic hourly sync for seamless updates. Publish to Power BI service - Training | Microsoft Learn

section: Design effective reports in Power BI
text: Which of the following statements about organizing items in folders inside a Power BI workspace is correct?

options.text: Folders are organizational units that help manage artifacts within a workspace.
options.explanation: Folders in Power BI workspaces serve as organizational units to help manage and categorize artifacts such as reports, dashboards, datasets, and dataflows. They allow users to group related items together for easier navigation and access within the workspace.

options.text: You can create nested subfolders up to 10 levels deep.
options.explanation: Power BI allows users to create nested subfolders within folders to further organize and structure their workspace. This hierarchical organization can be up to 10 levels deep, providing flexibility in how items are grouped and managed.

options.text: Items cannot be moved once they are placed in a folder.
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. In Power BI workspaces, items can be easily moved into folders and subfolders for better organization. This flexibility allows users to rearrange and restructure their workspace as needed to improve efficiency and accessibility of artifacts.

options.text: You can move single or multiple items into folders and subfolders.
options.explanation: Users have the ability to move single or multiple items into folders and subfolders within a Power BI workspace. This feature enables users to group related items together, making it easier to manage and access specific artifacts within the workspace. Remember: Folders are organizational only - they don’t change permissions or security. They are available in the Power BI Service (not in Desktop). They are especially useful in large workspaces with many reports and datasets.

explanation: Power BI now allows you to organize items (reports, datasets, dashboards, dataflows) into folders inside a workspace, making it easier to manage and navigate large collections of content. Purpose of folders Workspaces can quickly become cluttered as the number of reports, dashboards, and datasets grows. Folders provide a way to group related items together, improving discoverability and reducing confusion. Supported items You can organize reports, dashboards, datasets, and dataflows into folders. This helps teams separate content by project, department, or function. Collaboration benefits Multiple users working in the same workspace can easily find the content they need. Role-based access still applies - folders don’t override workspace permissions. Practical example In a Finance workspace, you might create folders like: Monthly Reports Quarterly Dashboards Dataflows for Compliance This way, analysts and managers can quickly locate the right content without scrolling through a flat list. Publish to Power BI service - Training | Microsoft Learn

section: Design effective reports in Power BI
text: You are a Power BI developer tasked with publishing a report from Power BI Desktop into a specific folder inside a workspace in the Power BI Service. However, when you attempt to publish, the option to select a folder does not appear in the dialog box. Which of the following actions will correctly resolve this issue?

options.text: Reinstall Power BI Desktop to enable folder publishing by default.
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Reinstalling Power BI Desktop will not enable folder publishing by default. The issue is related to a specific setting that needs to be configured to allow folder selection during publishing.

options.text: Enable the Publish dialogs support folder selection setting in the Preview features tab of the Options menu.
options.explanation: Enabling the Publish dialogs support folder selection setting in the Preview features tab of the Options menu will resolve the issue. This setting allows users to select a specific folder inside a workspace when publishing a report from Power BI Desktop.

options.text: Move the report manually into the desired folder after publishing, using the Power BI Service interface.
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Moving the report manually into the desired folder after publishing using the Power BI Service interface is a workaround but does not address the root cause of the issue. Enabling the folder selection option during publishing is a more efficient solution.

options.text: Upgrade your workspace to Premium capacity, since folder publishing is only supported there.
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Upgrading your workspace to Premium capacity is not necessary to enable folder publishing. The issue can be resolved by adjusting the settings in Power BI Desktop to allow folder selection during the publishing process.

explanation: To publish reports from Power BI Desktop to specific folders in the service, make sure that the Publish dialogs support folder selection setting is enabled in the Preview features tab in the options menu. Publish to Power BI service - Training | Microsoft Learn

section: Design effective reports in Power BI
text: Your manager asks you to set up a place in Power BI where the team can collaborate, organize reports, dashboards, and datasets in one central location. Which option best describes this feature?

options.text: A workspace is a feature in Power BI service that allows users to view reports only.
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. In Power BI, a workspace serves as more than just a viewing platform for reports; it acts as a collaborative hub where team members can work together on creating, organizing, and sharing reports, dashboards, and datasets.

options.text: A workspace is a centralized location or repository that allows you to collaborate with colleagues and teams to create collections of reports, dashboards, and so on.
options.explanation: The concept of a workspace in Power BI goes beyond simple report viewing; it functions as a central space where team members can collaborate, store, and manage various data-related assets such as reports, dashboards, and datasets. Create a workspace in Power BI - Power BI | Microsoft Learn Workspaces in Power BI - Power BI | Microsoft Learn

options.text: A workspace is a feature that allows you to view and edit the semantic model, build visualizations, and transform the data.
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. While a workspace in Power BI does offer functionalities for viewing and editing data models and creating visualizations, its primary purpose lies in providing a shared environment for team collaboration, report organization, and centralized data management.

explanation: Collaboration hub: A workspace is the central place where team members can work together on reports, dashboards, datasets, and dataflows. Organization: It acts as a container to keep all related Power BI content grouped logically. Role-based access: You can assign roles (Admin, Member, Contributor, Viewer) to control who can edit, publish, or just view content. Distribution: From a workspace, you can publish an app to share curated content with a broader audience. Power BI workspace - the central container for collaboration and organization of reports, dashboards, and datasets.

section: Design effective reports in Power BI
text: Which of the following statements about Power BI workspaces is correct?

options.text: Members have the highest level of control in a Power BI workspace, including managing roles and deleting the workspace.
options.explanation: Members in a Power BI workspace have the ability to create, edit, and delete content, but they do not have the highest level of control. They cannot manage roles or delete the workspace, as these permissions are typically reserved for the workspace admins or owners.

options.text: Contributors in a workspace can create, edit, and delete content, but they can't manage app publishing or workspace settings.
options.explanation: This statement is correct. Contributors in a Power BI workspace have the ability to create, edit, and delete content within the workspace. However, they do not have permissions to manage app publishing or workspace settings, which are typically reserved for members or admins.

explanation: Exam Tips: Contributor Role in Power BI Workspaces What they can do: Create new reports, dashboards, and datasets. Edit existing content in the workspace. Delete content they or others have created. Refresh datasets. Configure rowlevel security (RLS) in datasets. What they cannot do: Publish apps from the workspace. Update or manage app audiences. Change workspace settings (like permissions, capacity assignment). Add or remove users from the workspace. Overall Explanation Contributors = content creators/editors They cannot handle workspace governance tasks like app publishing or changing workspace settings. In short: Contributors are perfect for team members who need to develop and maintain reports/dashboards, but shouldn’t control distribution or governance.

section: Design effective reports in Power BI
text: Which of the following statements about Power BI Apps is correct?

options.text: Power BI Apps are only accessible to users who are members of the workspace where the app was created.
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Power BI Apps are not limited to users who are members of the workspace where the app was created. Apps can be shared with specific users or groups, allowing broader access to the app's content.

options.text: Once an app is installed, users must manually search for and open each dashboard or report separately.
options.explanation: This is incorrect option. Once a Power BI app is installed, users do not need to manually search for and open each dashboard or report separately. Apps provide a consolidated view of related content items, making it easier for users to access and interact with the shared content.

options.text: Apps in Power BI allow designers to share multiple related content items together, reducing the need to share them individually.
options.explanation: Power BI Apps are designed to allow creators to share multiple related content items together, such as dashboards, reports, and datasets. This reduces the need to share each item individually, providing a more organized and efficient way to distribute and access content within Power BI. Think of App like below: Ravi builds 5 HR reports and 2 dashboards in a workspace. Instead of sending links to each item, he publishes a single HR app. Priya and the HR team open the app and see all the content in one place, organized and consistent. In short: Apps = one package for multiple related Power BI items, making sharing easier and more reliable.

explanation:
Key Features of Power BI Apps:

Bundle content: Apps can include reports, dashboards, and semantic models (datasets) from a workspace.

Single distribution point: Instead of sharing each report or dashboard individually, designers publish one app that contains everything.

Tailored audiences: You can configure audience targeting so different groups see only the content relevant to them.

Always up to date: When the app is updated, all users automatically see the latest version without needing new links.

Governance: Apps ensure that users consume the official, curated version of reports, reducing duplication and confusion.
