text: What is the full form of DAX in Power BI?

options.text: A) Data Analysis Expressions
options.explanation: Data Analysis Expressions (DAX) is the full form of the acronym used in Power BI. It is a formula language and is used for creating custom calculations in Power BI to manipulate data and create advanced calculations.

options.text: B) Data Analytics Expressions
options.explanation: Data Analytics Expressions is not the correct full form of DAX in Power BI. DAX is specifically designed for data analysis and creating custom calculations, not general analytics.

options.text: C) Dynamic Analysis Expressions
options.explanation: Dynamic Analysis Expressions is not the correct full form of DAX in Power BI. DAX is primarily focused on data analysis and creating custom calculations, rather than dynamic analysis.

options.text: D) Data Access Expressions
options.explanation: Data Access Expressions is not the correct full form of DAX in Power BI. DAX is not related to data access but rather to data analysis and creating custom calculations in Power BI.

explanation: The full form of DAX in Power BI is: Data Analysis Expressions Data - Refers to the information you’re working with (tables, columns, values). Analysis - The calculations, aggregations, and logic you apply to understand that data. Expressions - The formulas you write, similar to Excel formulas, but designed for Power BI, SQL Server Analysis Services (SSAS), and Power Pivot in Excel. DAX is the formula language of Power BI. It lets you create measures, calculated columns, and tables to perform advanced calculations like yeartodate totals, running balances, or custom KPIs. Data Analysis Expressions (DAX) Reference - DAX | Microsoft Learn

text: State True or False: You can convert an entire semantic model from DirectQuery to Import, but not the reverse for a whole model (individual tables in a composite model can still switch storage mode more flexibly). In Import mode, all DAX functions are supported, while in DirectQuery mode some functions are restricted. DirectQuery mode always provides faster performance than Import mode because it queries the source directly. Composite models allow mixing Import and DirectQuery tables in the same dataset. When using DirectQuery, data is refreshed automatically every time a visual is interacted with. Import mode requires scheduled refreshes or manual refresh to update data. DirectQuery supports all time intelligence functions like SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR and DATESYTD. In Composite models, relationships can exist between Import tables and DirectQuery tables. Import mode stores data in memory, which can lead to faster calculations compared to DirectQuery. DirectQuery mode is recommended when working with very large datasets that cannot fit into memory.

options.text: False, True, False, False, True, True, False, True, True, True
options.explanation: This is incorrect option.

options.text: True, True, False, True, True, True, False, True, True, True
options.explanation: This is correct option. DirectQuery in Power BI: When to Use, Limitations, Alternatives - Power BI | Microsoft Learn Import Excel workbooks into Power BI Desktop - Power BI | Microsoft Learn Select a storage mode - Training | Microsoft Learn

explanation:
You can convert an entire semantic model from DirectQuery to Import, but not the reverse for a whole model.

True. Power BI allows converting an entire DirectQuery model to Import mode, but you can't toggle an entire Import model back to DirectQuery. This whole-model restriction is separate from composite models, where individual tables added through a DirectQuery-capable connection can switch between DirectQuery, Import, and Dual storage modes, as long as their applied transformations still fold.

In Import mode, all DAX functions are supported, while in DirectQuery mode some functions are restricted.

True. Import mode supports the full DAX library, while DirectQuery has limitations.

DirectQuery mode always provides faster performance than Import mode because it queries the source directly.

False. DirectQuery is often slower since every interaction sends a query to the database. Import mode is usually faster because data is cached in memory.

Composite models allow mixing Import and DirectQuery tables in the same dataset.

True. Composite models let you combine both modes in one dataset.

When using DirectQuery, data is refreshed automatically every time a visual is interacted with.

True. DirectQuery always queries the source in real time when visuals are used.

Import mode requires scheduled refreshes or manual refresh to update data.

True. Import mode stores a snapshot of data in memory, so refreshes are needed to update.

DirectQuery supports all time intelligence functions like SAMEPERIODLASTYEAR and DATESYTD.

False. Many time intelligence functions are limited in DirectQuery because they rely on calculations not always supported by the source.

In Composite models, relationships can exist between Import tables and DirectQuery tables.

True. Relationships can be created across Import and DirectQuery tables.

Import mode stores data in memory, which can lead to faster calculations compared to DirectQuery.

True. Import mode uses the VertiPaq inmemory engine, which is optimized for speed.

DirectQuery mode is recommended when working with very large datasets that cannot fit into memory.

True. DirectQuery is useful for very large datasets or when realtime access is required.
